claims.text: In as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films, magnetocaloric response and hysteresis are governed primarily by the density and mobility of grain boundaries and twin/phase interfaces.
Grain boundaries and twin/phase interfaces act as nucleation sites for the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Grain and twin boundaries can impede magnetic domain-wall movement.
Interfaces act as obstacles to propagation of the magnetostructural phase front.
Interface density and mobility control the breadth of the magnetostructural transition.
Interface density and mobility control hysteretic energy losses during the transition.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films are single-phase and ordered hexagonal.
The as-deposited films have a homogeneous microstructure with limited grain-boundary and interface density.
Annealing near 600 degrees Celsius for 5–30 minutes followed by rapid quenching will systematically modify grain size and interface density.
Annealing can change chemical ordering and composition partitioning in multicomponent magnetic alloys.
Changes in chemical composition and ordering during annealing can alter magnetic response.
Increasing grain-boundary and interface density lowers local nucleation barriers for the magnetostructural transition.
Increasing grain-boundary and interface density lowers barriers to propagation of the phase transition.
Increasing grain-boundary and interface density spreads the transformation over a broader temperature range.
Reducing abrupt domain-wall movement minimizes hysteresis.
Finer-grained processed films will have a broader magnetocaloric transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Finer-grained processed films will exhibit less hysteresis and lower transition-related energy dissipation than the as-deposited baseline.
As-deposited films exhibit a sharp, hysteretic first-order magnetostructural transition with a large magnetic entropy change.
The predictions apply near ambient temperature under low applied magnetic fields, provided composition and long-range chemical order remain unchanged.
Residual-stress changes caused by thermal processing may contribute to the magnetocaloric behavior.

contradictions.description: Interfaces are described as obstacles to phase-front propagation, while increased interface density is also said to lower propagation barriers. Their proposed effect on propagation is therefore internally inconsistent unless separate nucleation and pinning regimes are specified.

The controlled intervention fixes annealing temperature at approximately 600 degrees Celsius and varies duration, whereas the mechanistic prediction also relies on lower-temperature anneals; that variable is not included in the stated experiment.
